prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind O&M; scope to Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere); excludes public grid, non-farm port ops. Wildmere: boundary/dispatch/status; Export Limit Advisory when capability<target; applies accepted ceiling, records time. Turbine Controller (Glassfin): validated commands within protections, blocks conflicts, safe mode on auxiliary loss; Pitch Deviation Notice. Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor feed Turbine Sensor Bus. Offshore Substation (Morrowick): Main Transformer, export cable, Export Cable Monitor, station service transformers, Fire Detection Panel; Transformer Tap Snapshot→Shore Control Room; mode Substation Degraded. Substation Operator: approved switching, clearances, escalates alarms, notifies Grid Dispatcher. Emergency Generator (Foxglove): auto-start on auxiliary loss, no unapproved paralleling, sheds loads; Start Test Trace. SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale): time-stamped data→Shore Control Room (Amber Quay); Session Revocation Receipt→Cybersecurity Gateway. Shore Control Room: dispatch target/ramp, keeps last validated limit on grid comms loss. Grid Dispatcher: targets; priority safety>protection>export. Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard): Position Quality Flag. Mode Grid Constraint. Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown): Squall Window Bulletin, Deferred Task Rationale; survey dates; repair prioritization (severity, growth, weather, production); shows task duration/resources/dependencies. Duty Planner: mobilization (CTV/Daughter Craft/SOV/Helideck), Transfer Manifest Addendum→Vessel Master; assigns repair window, updates maintenance record, schedules follow-up; checks readiness vs departure window. CTV: Harness Audit Card. SOV: Recovery Basket Load Sheet. Storekeeper checks materials/tooling vs repair method. Weather Analyst: Wave Burst Record. Weather Service, Metocean Buoy. Port Agent: Berth Slot Confirmation. Marine Coordinator: berth occupancy/arrivals/departures view. Redoubt (permit control) blocks release. Vessel Master: Crew Count Correction. Personnel Tracking Console; North/South Access Scanner. Field Supervisor: briefing, confirms close-access findings documented, escalates→Marine Coordinator. Cybersecurity Gateway; Cybersecurity Analyst: Firmware Hash Attestation, evidence. Incident containment/recovery; SCADA Engineer validates restoration. Blade Inspection Drone (Larkspur): Leading Edge Tile Image. Close access only after isolation, rotor restraint, rescue verified; HSE Officer reviews method. Blade Specialist classifies defects,

New part:
S471: Weather Service forecasts are considered alongside berth availability because port conditions can delay loading or restrict vessel movement.
S472: The Weather Analyst produces the Visibility Confidence Note to summarize confidence in visibility conditions for near-term port and offshore planning.
S473: The Marine Coordinator uses the Berth Slot Confirmation to align an approved vessel arrival with the assigned berth window.
S474: Crew Transfer Vessel calls are coordinated to avoid conflicts at passenger access points and shared loading areas.
S475: Service Operations Vessel calls are planned with regard to draft, mooring requirements, and the time needed to prepare offshore stores.
S476: The Vessel Master confirms practical arrival and departure estimates against the vessel's operating limits.
S477: Port staging areas are reserved for equipment that must be inspected, secured, or transferred before sailing.
S478: The Warehouse System supports cargo preparation so that planned loads can be assembled before the vessel occupies the berth.
S479: The Storekeeper checks that critical spares are available and that packaging is suitable for marine transport.
S480: Work Permit Portal status is reviewed before departure so that required authorizations are not left unresolved at the port.
S481: The HSE Officer checks that access controls, emergency arrangements, and handling precautions are suitable for the planned activity.
S482: Personnel Tracking Console records are reconciled with the approved crew list before personnel board a vessel.
S483: The Marine Coordinator resolves competing berth requests by considering task urgency, vessel compatibility, and the consequences of delay.
S484: When berth capacity is constrained, lower-priority movements may be resequenced while preserving safe rest periods and required inspections.
S485: Fleet Dispatch Console schedules are updated to reflect confirmed changes to vessel availability and offshore task timing.
S486: Turnaround allowances include time to secure returned equipment, report defects, and prepare the vessel for its next assignment.
S487: Actual arrival, departure, and berth-occupancy times are recorded to improve future capacity estimates.
S488: During disruption, the Marine Coordinator reviews safe alternatives such as a later slot, a different suitable berth, or vessel standby.
S489: Coordination decisions and unresolved constraints are retained for operational review and the next planning cycle.
S490: Maintenance begins only after the work scope, access route, and responsible supervisor have been confirmed for the shift.
S491: The Duty Planner checks that the planned task matches the approved work authorization and that required personnel and equipment are available.
S492: The Work Permit Portal produces the Isolation Boundary Sketch.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
